results.evidence:
products/experiments/backend/experiment_saved_metric_service.py: `if existing_uuid:
    normalized_query["uuid"] = existing_uuid
else:
    # Create always mints a new uuid. Promoting an inline metric sends that
    # metric's query, uuid included. Keeping it puts the shared metric on the
    # same identifier as the inline copy...
    normalized_query["uuid"] = str(uuid4())`. The create path passes no `existing_uuid`, so it always falls into the `else` branch and overwrites any `uuid` supplied on the incoming query, while `normalized_query = dict(query)` preserves every other field of the submitted definition.

`update_saved_metric` computes `existing_uuid = saved_metric.query.get("uuid") if saved_metric.query else None` and calls `normalize_query_for_write(update_data["query"], existing_uuid=existing_uuid)`. Inside that function, `if existing_uuid: normalized_query["uuid"] = existing_uuid` keeps the stored uuid unchanged, and a mismatched incoming uuid still raises `ValidationError("Saved metric UUID cannot be changed")`.

In `update_experiment`: `saved_metrics_in_payload = "saved_metrics_ids" in update_data`; when true, `seen_metric_uuids |= self._collect_saved_metric_uuids(update_data["saved_metrics_ids"])` (the identifiers of the shared metrics being linked). Then `if not metrics_in_payload: self._dedupe_stored_inline_metrics(experiment, update_data, "metrics", seen_metric_uuids, rewrite=saved_metrics_in_payload)` and the same for `metrics_secondary`. `_dedupe_stored_inline_metrics` reads `stored = list(getattr(experiment, field) or [])` (already-stored inline metrics) and, when `rewrite` is set, runs them through `self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(stored, seen=seen)`, which regenerates any uuid found in `seen`. This runs for both `metrics` and `metrics_secondary` when only `saved_metrics_ids` is sent.

In `_dedupe_stored_inline_metrics`: `prepared = self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(stored, seen=seen)` then `if prepared and any(old.get("uuid") != new.get("uuid") for old, new in zip(stored, prepared)): update_data[field] = prepared`. When no stored uuid is in `seen` (no clash), `_assign_uuids_to_metrics` keeps every original uuid (`else: seen.add(original)`), so `prepared == stored` and `update_data[field]` is never set — leaving `experiment.metrics`/`metrics_secondary` and, since `_sync_ordering_with_metric_changes` only acts `if "metrics" in update_data`, the ordering arrays untouched too.

Once dedupe sets `update_data["metrics"]` with the regenerated uuid, `_sync_ordering_with_metric_changes` runs with `protected_primary_uuids` built from the (now-updated) `experimenttosavedmetric_set`, which includes the original uuid now owned by the attached shared metric: `removed = (old_uuids - new_uuids) - (protected_primary_uuids or set())`. Since the original uuid is in `protected_primary_uuids`, it is excluded from `removed`, so it is not stripped from `current_ordering`; meanwhile `added = new_uuids - old_uuids` contains the new inline uuid and gets appended: `for uuid in added: if uuid not in current_ordering: current_ordering.append(uuid)`. The ordering ends up containing both uuids.

Dedupe (`_dedupe_stored_inline_metrics`) only rewrites the inline metric dict in `update_data[field]`; it never touches `ExperimentToSavedMetric` rows or the saved metric's own `query`. The link creation/update loop (`saved_metric_serializer.save()` / `existing_link.save(...)`) runs from `saved_metrics_data` independently of the dedupe logic, so the shared metric keeps its stored uuid and the linked set is exactly what `saved_metrics_ids` requested.

SKILL.md now says: "create a shared metric with `experiment-saved-metrics-create` and attach that instead of keeping an inline copy on the experiment. Omit `uuid` from the query... If the experiment already has the inline metric, remove it from `metrics` or `metrics_secondary` in the same `experiment-update` that sets `saved_metrics_ids`." This replaces the old text that told agents to call `experiment-saved-metrics-create` with the same query and then just attach it.

When `metrics` is resent (`metrics_in_payload = True`) but `saved_metrics_ids` is not (existing link unchanged), `seen_metric_uuids` is populated from `experiment.experimenttosavedmetric_set` (the currently linked shared metric's uuid). Then `update_data["metrics"] = self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(update_data["metrics"], seen=seen_metric_uuids)` regenerates the clashing inline metric's uuid. In `_sync_ordering_with_metric_changes`, `protected_primary_uuids` (built from the still-linked shared metric) keeps the old clashing uuid out of `removed`, so it remains in the ordering while the new inline uuid is added.

result:
Inline and shared metrics on the same experiment no longer share an identifier, so each metric shows its own results.

Promoting an inline metric created a shared metric with `experiment-saved-metrics-create` and the inline metric's query, which already carried that metric's uuid. Create kept any uuid on the query. If the inline copy stayed on the experiment, both metrics used the same uuid, and results (matched by uuid) were attributed to the wrong metric. Create now always assigns a new uuid. Updates still keep the shared metric's existing uuid and still reject a change to it.

Attaching shared metrics was only checked against inline metrics when the update also resent those inline lists. An update that changed only `saved_metrics_ids` left stored inline metrics alone, so a shared metric with the same uuid could be attached and the clash slipped through. That update now runs the stored primary and secondary lists through the same dedupe used for inline metrics: shared-metric uuids stay fixed, and a colliding inline uuid is regenerated. Ordering keeps the shared metric's uuid and appends the new inline uuid. A saved-metrics update that does not collide leaves inline uuids as they are. Resending an inline list still dedupes that list, and a stored list the payload does not send is still reserved so the resent list cannot take its uuids.

Agent guidance for configuring experiment analytics no longer says to promote an inline metric by creating a shared metric with the same query and then attaching it. It tells agents to omit `uuid` when creating the shared metric, and to remove the inline metric from `metrics` or `metrics_secondary` in the same update that attaches the shared metric.

Tests cover a copied uuid being replaced on shared-metric create, a saved-metrics-only update regenerating a colliding primary or secondary inline uuid while leaving the other list and the shared metric's uuid unchanged, and a saved-metrics-only update leaving an already-distinct inline uuid in place.
